verdict: CMS Energy's Michigan utility business grew steadily, but a $525M write-down tied to restructuring its NorthStar clean-energy arm dragged GAAP profit down — adjusted EPS rose to $1.44 from $0.93.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs $0.92 a year ago — hit by NorthStar charges

kpis.label: Adjusted EPS
kpis.note: vs $0.93 a year ago, excluding the NorthStar items

segments.name: Electric utility
segments.note: Consumers Energy selling electricity in Michigan — the regulated core of the company, and its profit engine: $505M of operating income this quarter.

segments.name: Gas utility
segments.note: Consumers Energy selling natural gas in Michigan — smaller in summer, when heating demand is low.

segments.name: NorthStar Clean Energy
segments.note: Independent power generation outside the regulated utility. Revenue grew, but restructuring this business produced the quarter's big write-downs and a $510M operating loss.

opex.name: NorthStar impairment, disposal & exit costs
opex.note: Writing down NorthStar Clean Energy assets and paying to exit or dispose of parts of it as CMS restructures the business — the quarter's dominant one-off cost.

opex.name: Maintenance & other operating expenses
opex.note: Running and maintaining the power grid, gas network and plants day to day (the segment note reports $920M including the NorthStar impairment line above).

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of poles, pipes, plants and equipment over their working lives.

opex.name: General taxes
opex.note: Property and other taxes other than income tax — they rise as CMS invests more in its system.

otherDetail: A net $160M cost below operating profit: $214M of interest charges on CMS's debt, partly offset by $54M of other income (including $49M of non-operating retirement benefits and a $33M impairment of NorthStar equity investments).
footerNote: For this utility, cost of revenue is power supply: fuel for electric generation ($150M), purchased and interchange power ($596M), purchased power from related parties ($16M) and the cost of gas sold ($45M). The consolidated result was a $91M net loss — but $214M of losses (including NorthStar impairments) belonged to noncontrolling interests, so net income attributable to CMS Energy was $123M, and $121M was available to common stockholders ($0.39 per diluted share) after $2M of preferred dividends. Segment detail comes from the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q.

takeaways.title: One restructuring swallowed the quarter
takeaways.text: NorthStar Clean Energy took $525M of impairment, disposal and exit costs, plus a $33M write-down of equity investments. Operating income fell to $47M from $481M a year ago — almost entirely because of this one program.

takeaways.title: The regulated utility is healthy
takeaways.text: The electric utility alone made $505M of operating income and the gas utility $55M. CMS reaffirmed 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $3.83–$3.90 and 2027 guidance of $4.08–$4.17, targeting 6–8% long-term growth.

takeaways.title: Adjusted profit actually rose
takeaways.text: Stripping out the NorthStar items, adjusted EPS was $1.44 vs $0.93 a year ago. GAAP EPS of $0.39 and the adjusted figure describe the same quarter — the $1.08-a-share gap is the restructuring.

oneTimers: Asset impairment and restructuring at NorthStar Clean Energy: $525M of impairment, disposal and exit costs inside operating expenses, a $33M impairment of equity-method investments, and $456M pre-tax ($1.45 per share, $1.08 after tax) in CMS's reconciliation of GAAP to adjusted earnings.

Because much of NorthStar is owned with outside partners, $214M of the quarter's losses were attributable to noncontrolling interests — which is how CMS reports a $91M consolidated net loss yet $121M of income available to its own common stockholders.
